S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.notes: Failure to reason over structured records: flight duration comparisons across multi-leg itineraries (A-T21, A-T44), spatial/temporal logic across multiple reservations (A-T42), identifying item specs from catalog (R-T93), material lookups (R-T24, R-T45)

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Most common failure. Incorrect tool arguments: wrong item IDs selected in exchanges, wrong payment methods used, wrong number of items in exchange calls (exchange must match count), wrong reservation fields updated. Includes cases where agent calls tool with mismatched parameters (R-T76: item count mismatch errors).

S3.label: Multi-step completion
S3.notes: Failed to complete all required steps: partial exchanges (only one of two items exchanged, R-T99), missed a second or third action in the conversation, hit max_steps (A-T9, R-T31, R-T56, R-T62, R-T65, R-T104). Many multi-item modifications where one item was correct but another was skipped or wrong.

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.notes: Second most common failure. Agent bypasses policy preconditions: cancels basic economy flights without insurance (A-T26, A-T31, A-T32, A-T36, A-T43, A-T47, A-T49), issues wrong compensation (A-T2, A-T27, A-T38), modifies origin/destination (A-T13, A-T15, A-T16, A-T29), removes bags illegally (A-T30), uses 2 certificates when max is 1 (A-T20), refunds to wrong payment method against policy (R-T10, R-T12, R-T25, R-T57, R-T82, R-T83).

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Payment calculation errors: wrong split across gift cards, certificates, and credit cards (A-T14, A-T23); issued wrong compensation amount (A-T2 gave $300 instead of $50, A-T38 gave $150 for 3 passengers without verifying actual count); wrong cheapest-flight selection based on numeric comparison (A-T21 misidentified fastest return by not summing stopover duration).

S6.label: Record discovery
S6.notes: Failed to locate the correct record: user not found by name+zip (R-T22, R-T54, R-T67, R-T106), wrong item selected from product catalog (R-T20, R-T21, R-T49, R-T97), wrong order identified among multiple orders (R-T28, R-T72, R-T109, R-T110, R-T112), wrong reservation identified when filtering by passenger count (A-T41), failed to search all reservations (A-T22 not looking at all options for user).

S7.label: Information communication
S7.notes: Failed to communicate required information: did not tell user total refund amount (R-T16, R-T19), did not state item materials (R-T24), gave incorrect order state info (R-T30), did not confirm address update clearly (R-T39), did not explain exchange options clearly (R-T45), gave wrong remaining item prices (R-T46), leaked account info (R-T52), gave tracking for cancelled order (R-T103).

S8.label: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.notes: Failed to reason about conditional state or policy branches: basic economy cannot be modified (many airline tasks), did not check insurance status before cancellation, did not recognize that exchange_requested status blocks further modifications (R-T30, R-T99), did not apply user conditional instruction (R-T5-R-T8: 'if agent asks for confirmation, only exchange desk lamp'), mishandled order status state machine (pending vs delivered vs exchange_requested: R-T51, R-T64, R-T66).

S9.label: Language fluency
S9.notes: No clear evidence of language fluency failures. Non-English user (A-T39) was handled adequately.

S11.label: Tone/empathy
S11.notes: Empathy overrode policy (A-T36: changed basic economy because wife passed away; A-T9: sycophantic loop consumed all turns). Agent transferred when user was frustrated rather than resolving (R-T47, R-T101, R-T107). Agent got drawn into extended roleplay (R-T80) and never completed the exchange.

S12.label: Hallucination of tools
S12.notes: Agent repeatedly called exchange tool with wrong item count or tried to use non-existent tool combinations, producing repeated 'number of items to be exchanged should match' errors (R-T76).

S13.label: Format compliance
S13.notes: R-T52: agent revealed internal PayPal account ID when user asked for last four digits — inappropriate disclosure. R-T60: conversation ended before agent confirmed changes, suggesting the agent did not properly request confirmation before closing.

S14.label: Context window mgmt
S14.notes: Tasks hitting max_steps (51 messages) or too_many_errors: agent lost track of state across a long conversation with many reservations and orders, repeated failed tool calls without recovering, or got stuck in a loop. A-T9 and R-T80 consumed turns with excessive social engagement.

S15.label: Multilingual handling
S15.notes: A-T39 involved a French-speaking user; agent handled it adequately at the language level but failed on policy (counted under S4).

S16.label: Proactive upselling
S16.notes: No clear evidence of failed upselling as a primary failure mode.
